clue.text: Observe Hoffman character becoming upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the name is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Dustin Hoffman played Ted Kramer in the film Kramer vs Kramer

explanation.surface: Someone watches an actor's role turn sour as the character gets upset.
explanation.walkthrough: KRAMER turned upside down gives REMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to notice or comment on something, a synonym of observe as a verb.

clue.text: Move briskly in races to snatch gold up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards
snatching takes something into one's grasp, so the outer letters hold the other piece

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) races are the Isle of Man motorcycle races
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A runner hurries through races to grab a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait between walking and running, so to trot is to go at a brisk pace.

clue.text: Fish Greek character starts to cook hazardously in fat

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, placed within its letters

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, taken here from the next two words

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A Greek man fries fish dangerously in hot fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Men going over e-books about the first person from Asia

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
I is the first person pronoun
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Men read e-books about the first explorer from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going over' means placed on top; 'about' here only loosely means the first person comes before the e-books.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is a literary name for the East, the countries of Asia.

clue.text: Matinee idol's hat brother modelled

indicators.note: to model is to shape material into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A screen star's sibling posed wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee idol is a handsome actor adored by fans, which is what a heart-throb is.

clue.text: Goodbyes regularly written by some heartless American character on an epic journey

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

indicators.note: without its heart, a word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Farewell notes penned by an unkind American setting off on a long voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the hero of Homer's Odyssey, whose ten-year voyage home from Troy is the epic journey.

clue.text: Sinning, stealing a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: a thief takes the loot inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: erring means doing wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sinner pockets a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is an ornament worn on the earlobe, one item of jewellery.

clue.text: Stirring up a brawl during twilight wanting a change in the atmosphere

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it, so the jumbled letters go within
wanting means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: the gloaming is dusk; it loses its A, the clue's second 'a'

indicators.note: stirring mixes things together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out at dusk, and someone hopes the mood will change.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two a's: the first joins the brawl, the second is what twilight is wanting. Gloaming is a Scottish and poetic word for dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Global warming is the rise in the planet's temperature, a change in its climate and air.

clue.text: Help to catch large bird, one with a small brain

indicators.note: catching takes something into one's hold, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: aid is help
the rhea is a big flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone helps catch a big bird that is famously dim.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is informal for a silly, empty-headed person, as if their head held only air.

clue.text: Fantastic cinema drama about the Queen — it suggests all can gain fame and fortune

definitions.text: it suggests all can gain fame and fortune

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
fantastic means fanciful, unreal, so these letters take on a new form

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An extraordinary film about royalty promises riches and celebrity to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The American Dream is the national ideal that anyone, through hard work, can achieve success and prosperity.

clue.text: Eat rich hash including fine vegetable

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
a hash is a jumbled dish of chopped food, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A recipe advice: enjoy a rich chopped dish with a nice vegetable in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten, a vegetable.

clue.text: Very greatly regret flipping coins

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so sorry'
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone deeply sorry about tossing money away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping coins' reads as a coin toss, but flipping works on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of most of the European Union, issued as coins and notes.

clue.text: Mark Ronald's sandwiches: Scandinavian bread

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between slices, so the letters lie within the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two names

explanation.surface: Mark Ronald makes sandwiches with Nordic bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so Scandinavian bread is a Scandinavian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The krona is the currency of Sweden and the króna of Iceland, so it is Nordic money.

clue.text: Happening Conservative embraced by old money, finally to become leader of England

indicators.note: something embraced is held in another's arms, so it sits within the other letters
the final letter changes into a different one, swapping its last letter

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
currency is money

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A Tory, backed by old wealth, eventually rises to lead England.
explanation.walkthrough: C sits inside O + CURRENCY, and the final Y is swapped for E: OCCURRENCY becomes OCCURRENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence is an event, something that happens; happening as a noun means the same.

clue.text: Turn to realist philosopher

indicators.note: a turn changes the shape, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Advice to a thinker to become a realist.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Aristotle was the realist reacting against Plato's idealism.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, one of the founders of Western philosophy.

clue.text: Steal bundle of money back from airborne thief

parts.note: to jack is slang for to steal, as in hijack

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: Someone takes back a roll of cash from a flying thief.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small crow with a reputation for stealing shiny objects, so a thief on the wing.

clue.text: Zeus can perform lines

parts.note: can and john are both American slang for a toilet
to do is to perform
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: The king of the gods is able to recite his part.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeus is not the god here: Zeus faber is the scientific name of the fish called the John Dory.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory's Latin name is Zeus faber, so the genus name stands for the fish.

clue.text: Dresses king in neckwear that goes with casual shirt

parts.note: a T, as in a T-shirt, is a casual top

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the letters of the other

parts.note: ties are worn around the neck
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: A king puts on dresses with ties to match his T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual shirt' is read as 'a T', i.e. a T-shirt, a loose but fair device.
explanation.definitionFit: To attire someone is to clothe them, so attires is a verb meaning clothes or dresses.

clue.text: Train set's broken case

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them

indicators.note: something broken falls apart, so its letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A child's model railway is broken and needs a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train set' looks like one toy, but Train is a verb on its own; the ’s means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden box, originally for shipping tea, often used for moving house.

clue.text: Dense Democrat taking lead is not learned

parts.note: hard means dense, solid
an electrical lead is a wire
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A dim-witted Democrat in charge is not well educated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking lead' suggests heading a race, but lead is an electrical cable that D takes on before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardwired behaviour is innate, built into the brain from birth rather than acquired.

clue.text: Boot that is at the bottom of a hole in the ground

parts.note: a well is a shaft dug into the earth
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A boot lies at the bottom of a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'at the bottom of' puts the second piece below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is a wellington, a British word for a waterproof rubber boot.

clue.text: A bird oddly appearing in my closet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: showing up inside something means sitting within its letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, the first and third letters

parts.note: the first and third letters

explanation.surface: A strange bird turns up in someone's cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambry is an old word for a recess or cupboard, especially one in a church wall for sacred vessels.

clue.text: Middle Eastern country imprisons good man's lackeys

indicators.note: a prison holds someone inside, so the country's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Yemen is in the south of the Arabian Peninsula
S stands for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A Gulf state locks up a decent man.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are subordinates who always agree with the boss, servile followers like lackeys.

clue.text: Live and prosper without love

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: to do well is to prosper
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The Vulcan farewell 'Live long and prosper', but loveless.
explanation.walkthrough: DO WELL with its O removed leaves DWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside there, which is to live in the sense of having a home.

clue.text: Aliens kill that woman first with masses of cold water

parts.note: to ice is slang for to murder
she refers to a woman
ETs are extraterrestrials

explanation.surface: Space invaders murder a woman before anyone else, in a frozen landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is a placing instruction: the killing and the woman come before the aliens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice sheets are vast layers of frozen water covering land, as in Antarctica and Greenland.

clue.text: Overturn sack over spymaster in test

indicators.note: overturning something tips it over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to axe is to sack, to dismiss
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief is fired in an overthrow during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts EXA above M.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam, short for examination, is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Ordaining a priest, not foxtrot dancing!

indicators.note: not here means leave out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to frock is to make someone a cleric, the opposite of defrock
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A priest's ordination with no foxtrot, yet still a dance party!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxtrot' and 'dancing' look like one topic, but foxtrot is only the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocking means dancing to rock music, moving energetically to a beat.

clue.text: Economist, a Keynsian, conceals error

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep inside, out of sight, so the letters lie within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A Keynesian economist covers up a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is a wrong action or judgment, an error.
